messages:
michael: heads-up — nightly perf regression after we flipped the kernel-selector to prefer Triton fallback for 'tiny-head' cases. p95 latency on multi-stream workload jumped from ~95ms to ~140ms. allocating trace attached.

michael: profiler snippet:
```
> workload: gen/text, batch=8, max_seq=4096, heads=12, head_dim=64
p50: 72ms  p95: 140ms  tokens/sec: 5.2k
kernel path: flashattn -> triton_fallback (small-head path)
allocator: slab64 allocations skyrocketed (x4), reclaim stalls ~20ms, occasional transient OOMs reported by cuda-mempool
stack: runtime::workspace_alloc -> slab::alloc -> cublaslt_fallback (alloc wait)
OOM log: [2026-03-15T03:12:22Z] cuda OOM during allocate 12.3MB (retry)
```

sara: ugh. can you share the slab histogram and the mempool debug output? even a few lines will help.

michael: pasted top lines from mempool debug:
```
slab histogram: 32B: 102k | 64B: 410k | 128B: 160k | 256B: 12k | 1MB: 48
free lists skewed: 64B used 78% -> hot fragmentation for FFN scratch
reclaim loop count: 3 -> waited 18ms avg
```

dmitri: hypothesis: tiny-head triton path increases many small temporary buffers (packed q/k fragments + FFN scratch) and our slab64 growth combines with KVcache allocations to fragment GPU address space. fragmentation spikes cause more mempool churn -> allocator waits -> latency regression.

dmitri: quick repro: run 8 streams with heads=12, head_dim=64 and toggle kernel chooser to force FA vs Triton. FA wins for larger heads, but triton_fallback for <72 head_dim. maybe threshold tuned too high.

anne: can we try two quick mitigations?
1) increase default small-slab size from 64->128 for the failing config so FFN scratch uses fewer, larger blocks.
2) enable workspace coalescing for KV cache windows (coalesce adjacent small frees into bigger chunk).

michael: ran a lab build with slab default bumped to 128, simple test looks promising: p95 dropped to ~108ms (not all the way). mempool reclaim waits down to 6ms. but still seeing sporadic OOMs on long contexts (>12k tokens) when KV cache warms.

ben: let's not ship that as-is. we should add a canary rollout and telemetry to watch slab fragmentation ratio and reclaim_wait_ms. I can add a per-model gauge (model_id + kernel_path) to the console.

infra-bot: deploy starting: canary/runtime/small-slab-128 -> 3 nodes (eng-runtime-canary-4..6). CI passed.

anne: also want to adjust kernel-chooser tuning: add hysteresis so we don't flip per-request. change rule to prefer Triton only if estimated transient allocation < 256KB per token (heuristic). that should reduce small-buffer heavy paths.

michael: adding a short-term patch:
- bump slab small size to 128 for tiny-head profiles
- add coalesce pass on free for KV cache windows when contiguous free blocks detected
- change chooser threshold: triton_prefer_headdim < 48 -> previously was <72 (so we bias towards Flash for head_dim 48-72)

michael: action items:
- dmitri: run long-run (12hr) with slab128 + coalesce on staging and capture alloc histograms (ETA 6h)
- ben: add telemetry gauges + alert if reclaim_wait_ms > 25ms or fragmentation_ratio > 0.6 (ETA 3h)
- anne: prepare rollback patch for canary (revert chooser) in case error budget crosses threshold (ETA 1h)

sara: also capture KV cache allocation timeline. if coalesce helps we'll need to add unit tests around free-coalesce to avoid subtle correctness issues.

michael: noted. will post the bisection logs once long-run completes. thanks all. :thumbsup:
